summary: Shu-chen Chen worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2007) under Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang, and worked there as a teaching assistant in 1996.

Shubhachandra is an Indologist. He served as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and was affiliated with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (BA ~1961–1965; doctorate 1988) and under Shigeo Kamata. His career was spent at Komazawa University, progressing from assistant (1971) to professor (1984, 2014).

Shuhong Chang was a historian, archaeologist, and sinologist. He studied in France and China, taught at Zhejiang University and the National Beiping Art School, and held leadership roles at the Dunhuang Academy from 1942, becoming honorary director.

Shuichi Kato was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the University of British Columbia, Sophia University, and Free University of Berlin, and directed the Kyoto Museum for World Peace.
Shuichi Maida was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1928 to 1931 and was a student of Haya Akegarasu.

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar. His academic career includes appointments as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (2003) and as a researcher at Bukkyo University (2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (2006), and Musashino University (2006).

Shujiro Shimada was a scholar of Japanology, Sinology, and art history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1928 to 1931 and served on the faculty at Princeton University from circa 1962 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from Banaras Hindu University and Kyoto University, and later served as a Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University (attested 1998, 2010).

Shuken Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his education, including a doctorate in 2000, at Komazawa University, where he also held appointments from research assistant in 1976 to professor in 1991.
Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Northwestern University in 2014 under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn, having also studied under Weijue Shi.

Shuming Liang was a philosopher, Buddhist studies scholar, and Indologist. Educated at Shuntian Middle School, he joined Peking University's philosophy department in 1917 and founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and China Democratic League.

Shun Hidaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a research post at Otani University's Buddhism and Art Research Center in 2012 and served as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

Shun'ei Hirai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Komazawa University as professor (1964–1976), vice president (1986–1990), and emeritus professor (2001).
Shun'ei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi and served as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).
Shunei Tsuboi was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 1963 and 1972).

Shunkyo Katsumata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held faculty posts at Toyo University and served at Taisho University (~1944–1982), where he became an emeritus professor.
Shunpaku Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who served on the faculty at Shuchiin University, where he was an assistant professor in 1963 and a professor in 1976.

Shunpei Ueyama was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University (1941–1943). He later became a professor and emeritus professor at Kyoto University, director of the Kyoto National Museum, and president of Kyoto City University of Arts.

Shunryu Suzuki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji. He served as abbot of Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Soko-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.
